subject: Post-call: integration QA — chat vs completions, streaming semantics
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ivy Chen <ivy.chen@fastretail.com>, Tom Lopez <tom.lopez@fastretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap + outstanding integration questions

Hi Ivy / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and three follow-ups we promised to clarify so your infra team can validate feasibility: 

1) SDK & auth model — you indicated you prefer server-side SDK with service-account-style keys. We support client SDKs for experimentation but recommend server-side tokens for production. Monica attached a short design sketch (redwood-infra-design.pdf) showing our recommended pattern (server-side token minting + short-lived ephemeral tokens for edge services).

2) Routing & model variants — when you talked about prioritizing latency for checkout flows and lower-cost re-rankers for analytics, we suggested routing policy rules (by route path + user tier). See p.2 of the attached PDF.

3) Request/response schema questions — Tom asked about chat vs completions semantics, streaming behavior, and stop-token handling. Below are the concrete items we need answers to from your side so we can finalize a mutual action plan: 

  - For checkout assistance, do you expect incremental token-level streaming to the browser, or will you buffer server-side and return an assembled message?
  - Are you going to use structured tool-calling (e.g., call graphQL or product_search tools) or primarily free-text completions?
  - What maximum response size do you want enforced (approx max_tokens) and what stop sequences are required for your templates?

Next steps I propose: Monica (SE) will draft an integration checklist + sample request/response JSON based on your answers; I'll book a 45-minute follow-up to walk through the checklist and the proposed HA routing. I attached the initial plan workbook (postcall-mplan.xlsx).

Please reply with short answers to the three bullets above or mark a time on my calendar (Ivy, Tom).

Best,

—Aditya Rao

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + outstanding integration questions

Thanks, Aditya — good summary. A few clarifications from our infra side: 

- Streaming: for checkout we want token-level streaming to the browser for real-time UX — so low-latency per-token is important. We have a server-side aggregator but prefer the model to stream to our edge service which proxies to the browser.

- Tool calling / structured output: initially we will use a mix. We plan to call product_search and pricing_lookup tools from the model (structured responses with a small JSON schema) and then fall back to free-text completions. We care about deterministic JSON output so tool-calling + schema validation is needed.

- max_tokens / stop: for checkout suggestions, responses should be bounded — target upper bound ~256 tokens per response. We use custom stop sequences ("\n===END===\n") in some templates. Will Redwood enforce stop sequences deterministically in streaming mode?

Also: are there any tokenization differences we should be aware of between your hosted models and the open-model variants you recommend for Dedicated? We have some legacy templates that are token-sensitive.

Can Monica give us an example request/response for a streaming chat call with a tool call and a stop sequence included? That will help our engineers.

--Tom
Tom Lopez
Senior Platform Engineer, FastRetail
tom.lopez@fastretail.com

Tom / Ivy —

Appreciate the detailed notes. Below are concrete answers and an example payload (streaming chat with tool call + stop sequence). I kept the payload minimal so you can drop it into your test harness.

Short answers: 
- Streaming semantics: Redwood supports per-token streaming over HTTP/2 chunked responses and WebSocket. Stop sequences are enforced server-side; streaming will terminate once a stop token is emitted, but note: clients may receive an extra (partial) chunk due to network buffering — we provide a final 'done' event in the stream to indicate deterministic termination.

- Deterministic stop enforcement: Yes — the runtime will respect stop sequences, including custom separators like "===END===". For edge cases we also support a post-processing truncation hook on the server.

- Tokenization differences: Our hosted models and our recommended open-model variants use the same BPE tokenizer family with identical token counts for identical inputs. We publish tokenizer reference pages per model in the model catalog. If you have specific templates, we can run a tokenization trace and return token counts for each sample.

Example (minimal) streaming chat request w/ tool call and stop sequence — SDK pseudo-JSON: 

POST /v1/chat.stream 
Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral_token> 
Content-Type: application/json

Payload: 
{"model": "redwood-chat-7b", "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant for FastRetail."},{"role":"user","content":"Find top 3 products for user intent 'gift for mom'"}], "tools": [{"name":"product_search","schema":{"q":"string","limit":"integer"}}], "tool_call": {"name":"product_search","args":{"q":"gift for mom","limit":3}}, "stream": true, "max_tokens": 256, "stop": "===END===", "response_format": "structured-json"}

Streaming semantics notes: 
- Each chunk contains: {"token": "...", "cursor": <cursor-id>, "partial": true} and the backend will emit {"done": true, "final_summary": {...}} after the stop sequence is processed.
- For tool-calling, the tool result is emitted as a distinct event: {"tool_result": {"name":"product_search","value":{...}}} before generation resumes. 

Attachment: I added a small sample file with the example request + expected chunk sequence to the Drive link (see related_links). Also attached the infra diagram and the integration checklist I mentioned.

If you want, I can join your engineers for a 60-minute deep dive and walk the team through a live streaming example and a tokenization trace. Proposed slots tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks,

—Monica Patel
